countenance.meaning: A person's face or facial expression; support.
countenance.mnemonic: "Count the Nuance": Looking closely at someone's face to count the subtle expressions (nuances) on their countenance.

counterfeit.meaning: A fraudulent imitation of something else; fake.
counterfeit.mnemonic: "Counter + Fit": Giving fake notes at the counter that don't fit the legal standards.

covert.meaning: Not openly acknowledged or displayed; secret.
covert.mnemonic: "Covered": It sounds exactly like covered — a covert operation is completely covered up.

covet.meaning: Yearn to possess or have something belonging to someone else.
covet.mnemonic: "Covertly want it": You look at your friend's new car and covetously wish you could take it for yourself.

coy.meaning: Making a pretense of shyness or modesty that is intended to be alluring.
coy.mnemonic: "Toying": Acting shy and playing with a toy or your hair to look innocent.

crafty.meaning: Clever at achieving one's aims by deceitful or evasive methods.
crafty.mnemonic: "Craft": Someone who uses their craft (skills) not for art, but to trick people.

craven.mnemonic: "Cave in": A soldier who caves in instantly out of fear because he is craven.

credible.mnemonic: "Credit card": The bank only gives a credit card to someone who is credible (trustworthy).

crescendo.meaning: A gradual increase in loudness or intensity.
crescendo.mnemonic: "Increase-endo": Think of a musical beat that starts low and rises to a massive peak.

crestfallen.mnemonic: "Crest (Top) + Fallen": You were riding high at the crest of the wave, but then you fell down — totally disappointed.

croon.meaning: Hum or sing in a soft, low voice, especially in a sentimental manner.
croon.mnemonic: "Crow turning into a Peacock": Imagine a bird trying to sing a smooth, romantic melody softly.

cumbersome.meaning: Large or heavy and therefore difficult to carry or use; unwieldy.
cumbersome.mnemonic: "Kamra-some": A piece of furniture so big it takes up the whole kamra (room) and is tough to move.

cunning.meaning: Having or showing skill in achieving one's ends by deceit.
cunning.mnemonic: "Kan-kaatna": Someone so sharp they can kaat your kaan without you noticing.

curb.mnemonic: "Curb on the road": The concrete curb keeps the cars from driving off the road — it curbs them.

curmudgeon.mnemonic: "Car + Mud": An old, angry man whose car got stuck in the mud, making him highly irritated.

cursory.meaning: Hasty and therefore not thorough or detailed.
cursory.mnemonic: "Cursor": Moving your computer cursor lightning-fast across the screen just to skim a page.

curtail.mnemonic: "Cut the tail": Stripping down resources or time to shorten it.

daunting.meaning: Seeming difficult to deal with in anticipation; intimidating.
daunting.mnemonic: "Daantna": A task so massive it feels like a strict teacher daant-ing (scolding) you just by looking at it.

decorum.meaning: Behavior in keeping with good taste and propriety.
decorum.mnemonic: "Decorate the Room": When guests arrive, you decorate the room and maintain proper, polite manners (decorum).

decry.mnemonic: "Deep + Cry": Crying out loud in public to protest against something bad.

defame.meaning: Damage the good reputation of someone.
defame.mnemonic: "De (Down) + Fame": Pulling someone's fame down by spreading rumors.

deference.mnemonic: "Respect the Difference": Recognizing the difference in age or rank and showing high respect to an elder.

deflect.meaning: Cause something to change direction; turn aside.
deflect.mnemonic: "Reflect vs Deflect": Like a mirror reflects light, a shield deflects an incoming arrow away from you.

deft.meaning: Neatly skillful and quick in one's movements.
deft.mnemonic: "Deaf to Distractions": A master craftsman or coder who is so focused and deft with their hands that they are deaf to outside noise.

deify.meaning: Treat or worship someone as a god.
deify.mnemonic: "Deity": Turning a regular human into a deity (God) because you admire them too much.

deleterious.mnemonic: "Delete + Serious": Something so harmful that it causes serious damage, forcing you to delete it from your life.

deliberate.meaning: Done consciously and intentionally; carefully weighed.
deliberate.mnemonic: "Daily + Debate": Thinking so carefully that it feels like a daily debate in your mind before making a final choice.

delineate.mnemonic: "De-Line-Ate": Drawing a clear line on paper to show boundaries step-by-step.

delusion.meaning: A belief firmly maintained despite being contradicted by reality.
delusion.mnemonic: "Illusion in Mind": A permanent illusion stuck in your head making you believe things that aren't real.

demur.meaning: Raise doubts or objections; show reluctance.
demur.mnemonic: "Damn + Mur (Mudna)": Stopping right where you are, turning around (mudna), and saying, "Damn, I object to this!"

denigrate.mnemonic: "Degrade + Negate": Trying to negate someone's hard work and degrade their value in front of others.

denounce.meaning: Publicly declare to be wrong or evil.
denounce.mnemonic: "Announce the Crime": Making a loud public announcement that a politician or policy is completely corrupt.

deportment.mnemonic: "How you behave at the Airport/Port": Your behavioral etiquette (deportment) matters when you interact with authorities at a port.

depose.meaning: Remove from office suddenly and forcefully; testify.
depose.mnemonic: "De-Position": Kicking a dictator out of his royal position by force.

depravity.mnemonic: "Deep + Gravity": Someone sinking deep into the gravity of crimes and bad morals.

deprecate.mnemonic: "Depreciate Value": Looking down on an idea or criticizing it, lowering its importance (self-deprecating humor = making fun of yourself).

deride.mnemonic: "De-Ride": Making fun of someone so badly that you completely ruin their ride or confidence.

derivative.meaning: Imitative of the work of another person, and usually disapproved of for that reason.
derivative.mnemonic: "Derived from Calculus": Not original — something derived entirely from an existing formula or idea.

desiccate.meaning: Remove the moisture from something; cause to become completely dry.
desiccate.mnemonic: "Desert + Cake": Leaving a cake out in the hot desert sun until it becomes completely dry and crumbly.

despotic.mnemonic: "Boss + Dictator": A cruel, absolute ruler who acts like a ruthless boss over everyone.

desultory.meaning: Lacking a plan, purpose, or enthusiasm.
desultory.mnemonic: "Result-less Story": Jumping from one topic to another without a plan, leading to a result-less story.

detente.meaning: The easing of hostility or strained relations, especially between countries.
detente.mnemonic: "De-Tension": The absolute easing of tension between two warring nations.

deter.meaning: Discourage someone from doing something by instilling doubt or fear of the consequences.
deter.mnemonic: "Detergent bars the dirt": Like soap keeps dirt away, a heavy fine deters people from breaking traffic laws.

detract.meaning: Reduce or take away the worth or value of something.
detract.mnemonic: "De (Down) + Attract": Pulling the attraction or value of an achievement down by pointing out minor flaws.

detrimental.mnemonic: "Nutrient ka Ulta": Nutrients are good for health; something detrimental acts like a poison that ruins health.

deviate.meaning: Depart from an established course or standard.
deviate.mnemonic: "De-Route via Alternative": Turning away from the main highway to take a side road.

devious.meaning: Showing a skillful use of underhanded tactics to achieve goals; winding.
devious.mnemonic: "Devil-ish": A devious plan is a cunning, devil-ish scheme to trick someone.

dexterous.meaning: Showing or having skill, especially with the hands.
dexterous.mnemonic: "Dexter's Laboratory" / "Dexterity": Think of an expert scientist or coder who is incredibly quick and skilled with his hands.

diatribe.meaning: A forceful and bitter verbal attack against someone or something.
diatribe.mnemonic: "Die + Tribe": An angry speech wishing a whole tribe would die — a massive verbal teardown.

dichotomy.meaning: A division or contrast between two things represented as being opposed or entirely different.
dichotomy.mnemonic: "Di (Two) + Cut": Literally cutting something cleanly into two completely opposite halves.

dictate.mnemonic: "Dictator": Giving orders like an absolute ruler that everyone else must follow without question.

dictum.meaning: A formal pronouncement from an authoritative source.
dictum.mnemonic: "Dictator's words": An official, wise, or authoritative saying that is treated as law.

didactic.meaning: Intended to teach, particularly in having moral instruction as an ulterior motive.
didactic.mnemonic: "Didi + Act": Your elder Didi always acting like a school teacher, trying to give you life lessons and moral lectures.

diffident.meaning: Modest or shy because of a lack of self-confidence.
diffident.mnemonic: "Difficult to Confide": Someone who finds it difficult to talk to people because they lack confidence.

diffuse.meaning: Spread out over a large area; not concentrated.
diffuse.mnemonic: "Diffuser": Like a room freshener diffuser that spreads a scent widely across the entire hall.

digression.meaning: A temporary departure from the main subject in speech or writing.
digression.mnemonic: "Diversion on Highway": Leaving the main topic during a lecture to tell a random story, then coming back.

dilatory.meaning: Slow to act; intended to cause delay.
dilatory.mnemonic: "Delay-tory": Doing tasks so slowly that you deliberately cause a delay.

dilettante.meaning: A person who cultivates an area of interest without real commitment or knowledge.
dilettante.mnemonic: "Dil se thoda sa": Someone who dabbles in coding, photography or music just for fun (dil se), but isn't a serious professional.

diminutive.mnemonic: "Diminish": Something that has diminished in size so much that it has become tiny.

dirge.meaning: A lament for the dead, especially one forming part of a funeral rite.
dirge.mnemonic: "Die + Song": A sad song sung when someone has died.

discernible.hindiMeaning: Saaf dikhne wala / Pehchana jaane yogya
discernible.mnemonic: "Discoverable": Clear enough to be noticed or discovered by the eyes or mind.

disciple.meaning: A personal follower of a teacher, philosopher, or religious leader.
disciple.mnemonic: "Discipline": A student who follows a master with strict discipline.

discomfit.meaning: Make someone feel uneasy or embarrassed.
discomfit.mnemonic: "Dis-comfort": Literally putting someone out of their comfort zone and making them blush or sweat.

disconcerting.mnemonic: "Dis-concert": If the music stops suddenly during a live concert, the sudden silence is highly disconcerting.

discount.meaning: Regard a possibility or fact as being unworthy of consideration; reduce price.
discount.mnemonic: "Dismiss the Count": Throwing an idea out of calculations because you think it's highly unlikely.

discreet.meaning: Careful and circumspect in one's speech or actions, especially to avoid causing offense.
discreet.mnemonic: "Secret Keeper": Being quiet and careful so secrets don't leak — the double 'e' looks like two closed eyes keeping a secret, unlike discrete which means separate.

discrepancy.meaning: An illogical or surprising lack of compatibility between two or more facts.
discrepancy.mnemonic: "Difference in Receipt": A mismatch between the money you spent and the amount written on the final bill.

disdain.meaning: The feeling that someone or something is unworthy of one's consideration or respect.
disdain.mnemonic: "Dis-respect the Stain": Looking down on someone with absolute contempt, treating them like a dirty stain.

disentangle.meaning: Free something from an entanglement; extricate.
disentangle.mnemonic: "Dis + Tangle": Untangling a messy knot of wires or a complicated situation.

disingenuous.meaning: Not candid or sincere, typically by pretending that one knows less about something than one really does.
disingenuous.mnemonic: "Dis (Not) + Genuine": Someone who pretends to be innocent but is secretly playing a game.

disinterested.meaning: Not influenced by considerations of personal advantage; unbiased.
disinterested.mnemonic: "Distance from Interest": A judge who keeps his personal profits away from a case so he can remain completely fair (not the same as bored/uninterested).

dismantle.meaning: Take a machine or structure to pieces.
dismantle.mnemonic: "Mantelpiece nikalna": Taking an entire engine or structure apart piece by piece.

disparate.meaning: Essentially different in kind; not allowing comparison.
disparate.mnemonic: "Dis-separate": Keeping things completely different and separate because they don't match.

dispense.meaning: Distribute or provide a service or information; manage without (dispense with).
dispense.mnemonic: "Dispenser": Like a sanitizer dispenser giving out soap, or dispensing with old rules (throwing them away).

disperse.meaning: Distribute or spread over a wide area.
disperse.mnemonic: "Dis-purse": If a purse snaps open on the street, all the coins disperse (scatter) everywhere.

dissemble.meaning: Conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.
dissemble.mnemonic: "Dis-assemble your real self": Hiding your true, angry face behind a fake smile to fool people.

disseminate.mnemonic: "Discuss via Internet": Blasting information, news or knowledge across the web so millions see it.

dissent.meaning: The expression or holding of opinions at variance with those officially held.
dissent.mnemonic: "Dis-sentiment": Going completely against the popular sentiment, or voting "No" when everyone else votes "Yes".

dissident.meaning: A person who opposes official policy, especially that of an authoritarian state.
dissident.mnemonic: "Dis-Sident (sidhe baithne ka ulta)": A rebel who refuses to sit down quietly and actively protests against the government.

distend.meaning: Swell or cause to swell by pressure from inside.
distend.mnemonic: "Distance + Extend": A stomach or balloon extending its size and expanding outwards due to gas or water.

distill.meaning: Extract the essential elements of something; purify a liquid.
distill.mnemonic: "Distilled Water": Boiling away the waste to extract only the purest, most concentrated essence of a topic or liquid.

distort.meaning: Pull or twist out of shape; give a misleading account of.
distort.mnemonic: "Dis-torture the truth": Twisting facts or a picture so much that the original shape and meaning is ruined.

distressed.meaning: Suffering from anxiety, sorrow, or pain.
distressed.mnemonic: "Stress extreme level": Being deeply troubled, heartbroken, or facing a highly stressful emergency.

divergent.meaning: Tending to be different or develop in different directions.
divergent.hindiMeaning: Binn / Alag disha mein jaane wala
divergent.mnemonic: "Diverge": Lines or opinions that start at the same point but split up and head in totally opposite directions.

divorced.mnemonic: "Divorce": Permanently separated from reality or from another entity — his theories are completely divorced from reality.

divulge.meaning: Make known private or sensitive information.
divulge.mnemonic: "Die + Vulg (vulgar secret)": Promising you won't reveal a secret until you die, but then divulging (leaking) it to everyone.

doctrinaire.meaning: Seeking to impose a doctrine in all circumstances without regard to practical considerations.
doctrinaire.mnemonic: "Doctor of Rules": A rigid person who stubbornly insists on following bookish theories, completely ignoring reality.

documentary.meaning: Consisting of official written or printed matter; a factual film.
documentary.mnemonic: "Documents": Based entirely on solid, real-life documents and facts rather than fiction.

dogged.meaning: Having or showing tenacity and grim persistence.
dogged.mnemonic: "Dog-like chase": Chasing a goal relentlessly, like a hunting dog that absolutely refuses to give up the scent.

dogmatic.meaning: Inclined to lay down principles as incontrovertibly true.
dogmatic.mnemonic: "Dog is Must": My way is the only right way — rigidly imposing your beliefs on everyone else.

dormant.meaning: Having normal physical functions suspended or slowed down for a period of time.
dormant.mnemonic: "Dormitory": Like students sleeping soundly in a university dormitory — a volcano or virus that is currently inactive but alive.

dowdy.meaning: Unfashionable and without style in appearance.
dowdy.mnemonic: "Dull + Lady": Dressing in old, sloppy, unfashionable clothes that lack colour or sharpness.

draconian.mnemonic: "Dracula's Laws": Imagine Dracula becoming the prime minister and passing terrifyingly cruel, severe punishments for tiny mistakes.
